headline: US Employment Increases by 165,000 in October
summary: U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, while the national unemployment rate declined to 4.1%.
why: The U.S. labor market report is a primary indicator of economic health, heavily influencing Federal Reserve interest rate policy and market expectations for inflation.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Stronger-than-expected job growth can signal economic resilience but may also fuel concerns about persistent inflation and higher interest rates.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Labor market data directly impacts the Federal Reserve's outlook on interest rates, which is the primary driver for equity and bond market valuations.
